text:
G2 is a spec update. In code, a judge launch with no MCP view passes `--disallowedTools "mcp__*"` and no `--strict-mcp-config`, and ECC-B10 says the same. Only the tool-less session reviewer already passes `--strict-mcp-config`.

- **ECC-B10 wording:** `executor-claude-code.spec.md:73` says a judge launch sends "`--disallowedTools "mcp__*"` when there is no MCP view, else the strict private MCP config of ECC-B3". `--strict-mcp-config` appears only in the "else" branch.
- **ECC-B10 scenario:** the one scenario (line 75) says only that the argv holds no write tool, no step rule, no `--fallback-model` and no `--resume`.
- **ECC-AC7 (line 140):** it covers the MCP-view case only: `--strict-mcp-config` with a private config, no `--disallowedTools "mcp__*"`. No criterion covers the no-view case.
- **ECC-AC4 (line 137):** a judge launch never has a write tool, a step allow rule, `--fallback-model` or `--resume`.
- **Judge code, `claude.py` `judge_argv` (lines 187-204):**
  - Tool-less views (lines 194-196): `--tools ""`, `--strict-mcp-config`, `--disallowedTools mcp__*`, `dontAsk`. This is the session reviewer, SRV-B18 to B20.
  - MCP views with a private config (lines 199-201): `--strict-mcp-config --mcp-config <cfg>`, with no `mcp__*` deny.
  - No-view fallback (lines 202-203): `--disallowedTools mcp__*` and no `--strict-mcp-config`.
  - This fallback is also used when views hold MCP tools but `mcp_config` is `None`.
- **Tests:**
  - `test_claude_executor.py:85-93` (judge read-only) asserts `--disallowedTools == "mcp__*"` for a plain judge and does not assert on `--strict-mcp-config`.
  - Lines 96-111 (ECC-AC7) assert the strict private config for MCP views. Lines 108-111 assert the no-config fallback keeps `mcp__*` and has no `--mcp-config`.
  - `test_session_review.py:598` asserts `--strict-mcp-config` for the tool-less reviewer.
- **Task note:** `batch-queue/tasks/i21.md:22` says today's ordinary judge launch shows about 1,350 tokens of connectors. Line 29 sets criterion 3: every judge launch passes `--strict-mcp-config`, and a judge with MCP views still gets its views. Line 21 says `--strict-mcp-config` alone, with no `--mcp-config`, is enough.
- **Research:** `claude-code-cli-headless.rsrch.md:46` (F15) and `:63`, and `executor-capability-matrix.rsrch.md:32` and `:35`, name `--strict-mcp-config` as the way to restrict MCP.
- **Needed:** reword ECC-B10 so the flag is sent in every case, add a no-view scenario, and extend ECC-AC7 or add a criterion for the no-view and no-config cases. Code change: add the flag at `claude.py:202`. The existing tests at test_claude_executor.py:85-93 and 108-111 would need updates.

ARTIFACT gap_finding: Spec `plugins/tempergraph/docs/specs/executor-claude-code.spec.md`: ECC-B10 (line 73) says a judge sends `--disallowedTools "mcp__*"` when there is no MCP view, else the strict private config of ECC-B3, so `--strict-mcp-config` is only in the "else"; its one scenario (line 75) and ECC-AC4 (137) don't cover it; ECC-AC7 (140) covers only the MCP-view case; no criterion covers the no-view case. Code `plugins/tempergraph/engine/src/tempergraph/executors/claude.py` `judge_argv` 187-204: tool-less reviewer (194-196) already has `--strict-mcp-config` plus the `mcp__*` deny; MCP views with a config (199-201) have `--strict-mcp-config --mcp-config` and no deny; the no-view fallback (202-203, also used when views hold MCP tools but `mcp_config` is None) has the deny and no `--strict-mcp-config` (read). Tests `engine/tests/test_claude_executor.py` 85-93 (plain judge: `--disallowedTools` is `mcp__*`, strict flag not asserted), 96-111 (ECC-AC7 MCP case; no-config fallback keeps `mcp__*`, no `--mcp-config`), `test_session_review.py:598` (tool-less reviewer has the strict flag). Task note `batch-queue/tasks/i21.md` 21-22, 29 (criterion 3), `docs/tasks/i21.triage.md:27` (G2). Research `claude-code-cli-headless.rsrch.md` 46, 63 and `executor-capability-matrix.rsrch.md` 32, 35. Needed: reword ECC-B10 (flag in every case), add a no-view scenario, extend ECC-AC7 or add a criterion for the no-view and no-config cases, and update the tests above.
